p: Born Bahadur Khan into the Muzaffarid dynasty, he was the son of Prince Khalil Khan, who became sultan in 1511 as Muzaffar Shah II, and of Rani Lakshmi Bai, daughter of a Gohel Rajput. His grandfather, Sultan Mahmud Begada, kept him at court. When his elder brother Sikandar Shah was named heir, Bahadur Khan feared for his life and fled, first to Chittor and then to Ibrahim Lodi; he was present at the Battle of Panipat without taking part in the fighting.

Muzaffar Shah II died in 1526. Sikandar Shah was murdered after a few weeks on the instructions of his slave Imad-ul-Mulk Khush Kadam, who put an infant brother on the throne as Mahmud Shah II. Bahadur Khan returned, the nobles joined him, and he marched on Champaner, executed Imad-ul-Mulk and had the child poisoned.

Bahadur Shah campaigned in the Deccan in 1528 and 1529, taking the fort of Ahmednagar and forcing the rulers of Ahmadnagar and Berar to sign a humiliating treaty. The fortress of Mandu fell on 28 March 1531, when Sultan Mahmud Shah II of Malwa and his seven sons were captured; they were later put to death by their guards during a rescue attempt. In 1532 he raised a siege of Chittor in return for an enormous ransom. Until his defeat by Humayun the power of Gujarat was at its height, with the rulers of Ahmednagar and Burhanpur acknowledging him as overlord.

The quarrel with Humayun began because Bahadur Shah had sheltered the Mughal prince Muhammad Zaman Mirza. The rout near Mandasur is usually explained by the treachery of Rumi Khan, the Turkish head of the Gujarat artillery. Bahadur Shah fled to Mandu, Champaner and finally Diu. When Humayun left to face the revolt of Sher Shah Suri, the country rose, and Bahadur Shah defeated the Mughals at Kanij and expelled them from Gujarat.

The Treaty of Bassein was signed on 23 December 1534 aboard the galleon St. Mattheus. Having recovered his kingdom, Bahadur Shah regretted the alliance. In February 1537 he visited the Portuguese viceroy's ship off Diu and was attacked and killed on his way back, on 13 February; his body was thrown into the sea. According to the Mirat-i-Sikandari, the viceroy had intercepted his message inviting the Deccan sultans to ally against the Portuguese. He left no son, and after his chosen heir, his nephew Miran Muhammad Shah of Khandesh, died on the way to Gujarat, the nobles chose Mahmud Shah III, son of his brother Latif Khan.

notes: Conflicts in the article: the lead says Gujarat 'came under attack of Humayun and fell' in 1532 and that he reigned 1526-1535 and 1536-1537; the body dates the quarrel to 1532, the fall of Chittor and the defeat to March 1535, and gives no year for the recovery. I gave no year for the defeat or recovery.
The article says he 'ascended the throne in 1527' after his father's death in 1526; the existing entry says 1526. I gave only the father's death year.

The body says he was killed 'on his way back' from the viceroy's ship; the existing description says 'during a meeting on a Portuguese ship'. The article calls the Portuguese commander 'the viceroy' without a name at this point (Nuno da Cunha is named only for 1531), so I did not name him.
The article's story of his killing Rana Sanga's nephew in exile and the tale of the heap of salt were left out.
